CWE-89.name: SQL Injection
CWE-89.officialName: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection')
CWE-89.description: Constructing SQL queries via string concatenation, template literal interpolation, or unparameterized input allows attackers to manipulate query logic, exfiltrate data, or modify database records.
CWE-89.remediation: Use parameterized queries or prepared statements (e.g., `db.query('SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?', [userId])`) or a query builder/ORM with bound parameters instead of concatenating user input.

CWE-79.name: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
CWE-79.officialName: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')
CWE-79.description: Writing untrusted or dynamic data into dangerous DOM sinks such as innerHTML, outerHTML, document.write(), or jQuery .html() without sanitization enables arbitrary script execution in users' browsers.
CWE-79.remediation: Use safe DOM APIs such as `textContent` or `innerText` instead of `innerHTML`/`document.write()`. When HTML rendering is required, sanitize with a vetted library like DOMPurify.

CWE-78.name: Command Injection
CWE-78.officialName: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')
CWE-78.description: Passing unvalidated or dynamically constructed strings into OS command execution functions (such as child_process.exec or spawn with shell: true) allows attackers to execute arbitrary system commands.
CWE-78.remediation: Avoid shell invocation when possible. Use `execFile` or `spawn` with an explicit argument array and `shell: false`, and strictly validate or allowlist any user-controlled parameters.

CWE-798.name: Hardcoded Secrets
CWE-798.description: Embedding API keys, passwords, tokens, private keys, or database credentials directly in client-side or server-side JavaScript exposes sensitive secrets to anyone who can inspect the source code.
CWE-798.remediation: Remove secrets from source code immediately, rotate exposed credentials, and load sensitive values from environment variables or a dedicated secrets manager on the server side.

CWE-95.name: Insecure eval()
CWE-95.officialName: Improper Neutralization of Directives in Dynamically Evaluated Code ('Eval Injection')
CWE-95.description: Using `eval()`, `new Function()`, or string-based `setTimeout()`/`setInterval()` evaluates strings as executable JavaScript, creating severe code injection and XSS risks if any dynamic input reaches it.
CWE-95.remediation: Replace `eval()` with safe alternatives such as `JSON.parse()` for data parsing, function maps for dynamic dispatch, and pass callback functions rather than code strings to `setTimeout()`/`setInterval()`.
